project: History2 Korean History II learning webapp
status: high-risk historical wording audited and corrected

methodology.day1_to_day6: Reuse existing 140-question structural/source mapping audits, then perform high-risk terminology, chronology and causal-framing spot audit on student-facing content.
methodology.day7_to_day18: Direct review of question stems, options, answer keys, explanations, recovery clues, O/X corrections and source-boost test questions.
methodology.verification: High-risk claims cross-checked against authoritative historical/public records sources before correction.
methodology.principle: Preserve question IDs, answer indices and learner history unless a verified answer-key error is found. Correct misleading simplification at explanation/recovery level first.

fast_content_precision_patches.change: Clarified direct military-government rule and non-recognition of Korean political organizations as official governments.
Clarified the UN commission-observation principle and actual election in South Korea under UN observation.

fast_content_precision_patches.topic: Special Investigation Committee of Anti-National Activities
fast_content_precision_patches.change: Added government opposition/noncooperation and the 1949 police attack as major reasons for weakened activity.
Expanded context from the 1947 police shooting through 1948 conflict, armed uprising, suppression and civilian casualties.
Specified the January 1950 Pacific defense-perimeter context and prevented teaching the speech as a sole cause of the Korean War.
Clarified UN Security Council resolutions, member-state military support and U.S.-led unified command.
Reworded to Park Chung-hee's eligibility to seek a third presidential term.

fast_content_precision_patches.topic: Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea
fast_content_precision_patches.change: Changed 'central city' to the city where it was established in 1919 and noted later movement through China and settlement in Chongqing in 1940.
Aligned test remediation with the fuller historical context used in the main learning flow.

unit1_precision_patches.change: Clarified that early rules required active-duty generals/admirals, the 1919 revision allowed civilian appointment in law, while all actual governors-general remained military-background figures.

runtime_application.adaptive_day7_to_day18_review: same source boosts and accuracy patch are loaded before adaptive_fast_review.js
runtime_application.day1_to_day6: unit1_content_accuracy_patch.js is loaded only on detailed student flows through sync_local_hook.js

source_context_rule.priority_1: Show exact textbook/workbook page only when an existing source label or source image filename provides a reliable page number.

limitations: A structural/source audit does not by itself prove historical accuracy.
Historical interpretation can differ by textbook and scholarship; the audit prioritizes broadly established factual chronology, institutional descriptions and neutral causal wording.
This audit does not claim that every sentence in Day 1-18 has been independently source-cited line by line.
Future textbook-edition-specific page mapping should be added only from verified source metadata.
